newsitem.title: BELGIUM: INNOGENETICS HAD 1996 LOSS DUE ACCOUNT CHANGE.
newsitem.headline: INNOGENETICS HAD 1996 LOSS DUE ACCOUNT CHANGE.

text.p: Belgian biotechnology firm Innogenetics NV , which is listed on the small cap market Easdaq, said on Sunday it had a 105 million franc ($3.4 million) 1996 loss instead of a 51.8 million ($1.7 million) profit because of an accounting adjustment.
The company said in a statement that on March 22 it was advised by its auditors that it should adjust its accounts to a recent change in U.S. accounting requirements.

"The board of Innogenetics decided to comply fully with the U.S. GAAP amendments, which provide that the difference between the exercise price of the warrants issued one year prior to the IPO and the IPO issue price be considered as an expense and an equivalent increase of the capital paid-in," the statement said.
It added that the equity of the company is not affected by these adjustments nor are the previously reported operating results.

Innogenetics said on March 5 that 1996 turnover rose 54 percent to 829.8 million Belgian francs. Net income for 1996 was reported at 51.8 million francs, compared to a net loss of 114.4 million in 1995.
Innogenetics, which sells diagnostic tests for diseases such as HIV and Alzheimers, targets five disease areas: infectious diseases, tissue repair, immune and neurodegenerative and genetic disorders.
